scope: Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Chapter 19 (with Chapter 11 and 14 claims and Online Appendix A1.6, A3 and A4): Monetarism. Monetary and fiscal regimes, NI-7 observational equivalence and double-passive indeterminacy; open-market-operation claims of Chapter 11 and the helicopter arithmetic; Cagan money demand under rational expectations with the full solution family, sunspots and fiscal selection of the price level; money in the utility function with FOCs derived from optimisation under perfect foresight and on a finite event tree, the value of money, power utility and certified Figure 19.1 numbers (E13: 1 + mu > beta); global money-targeting dynamics; unpleasant arithmetic; seigniorage, the Laffer peak (E16) and Baumol-Tobin elasticities; pruning deflations (E17: TVC fails iff mu >= 0) and inflations (finite-time explosion, countably many equilibria, modified utility); Obstfeld-Rogoff redemption and Cochrane's demonetised equilibrium (E18 caption corrected); nonseparable utility (E19: stable iff b > 1 + i/2); cash in advance with the stochastic Euler equation derived from optimality ((19.29) needs the money TVC, (19.38) corrected, E14, E15); continuous-time money with CES limits (E20) and the IS curve with money (E21). Printed errors corrected with Lean counterexamples.
source: John H. Cochrane, The Fiscal Theory of the Price Level, Princeton University Press, Chapter 19, pp. 433-464, Chapter 11, pp. 315-318, Section 14.1, p. 342, and Online Appendix A1.6, A3.1-A3.2 and A4, pp. 567-569, 612-632 and 635-641.
